How to fix ↓ Background Apache Log4j is a widely used logging library for Java applications, providing a reliable and flexible logging framework. It supports various logging configurations, including the ability to secure connections through TLS. The verifyHostName attribute was introduced to enhance security by ensuring that the hostname in the certificate matches the hostname of the server being connected to. However, a flaw in versions 2.12.0 to 2.25.3 led to this attribute being ignored, exposing applications to potential man-in-the-middle attacks. Vulnerability Detail The vulnerability arises from the incomplete fix for CVE-2025-68161, which only addressed hostname verification when enabled via the log4j2.sslVerifyHostName system property. The verifyHostName attribute in the <Ssl> element was ignored in versions 2.12.0 through 2.25.3, leaving TLS connections vulnerable to interception. An attacker could exploit this flaw if they could present a trusted certificate, allowing them to perform a man-in-the-middle attack when using SMTP, Socket, or Syslog appenders with TLS configured through the <Ssl> element. However, this is not recommended as it compromises security.
